records.date_label: Public project account; event date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Founder-reported project history; no independent outcome measurement.
records.summary: The public founder account describes connecting Bee context to ChatGPT and developing a Daily Command Center to sort commitments, delegated work, changes, and unresolved decisions. Its usefulness is founder-reported.
records.title: Capture meets a daily workflow

records.date_label: Public project account; event date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Founder-reported problem statement, not a measured comparison.
records.summary: The founder describes returning to later conversations with facts still available but too much prior reasoning missing: why an assumption changed, what failed, and what remained uncertain. That distinction defines the continuity problem in the published origin story.
records.title: The understanding had to be rebuilt

records.date_label: Public project account; event date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Documented project rationale; the complete portable product remains unfinished.
records.summary: The public story identifies Lyra Core as the personal reference experience and Wildline as the effort to extract reusable mechanisms. The portability question is how another person could develop their own continuity without inheriting the founder's history.
records.title: A question beyond one personal system

records.date_label: Published architecture; historical date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Documented design boundary; not a claim of universal live ingestion.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: The documented architecture separates source observations from interpretations and permission. Captured information can inform a later answer while uncertainty remains visible and the user retains decision authority.
records.title: An observation still needs judgment

records.date_label: Continuity note documented 2026-09-28; original discussion date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Documented governance principle; not a new authority grant.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed continuity record and the public architecture give current explicit user direction and source evidence priority over older interpretations. Preserving history is useful only if a later correction can change what carries forward.
records.title: Earlier context can become stale

records.date_label: Exploratory observation documented 2026-10-17
records.epistemic_status: Documented exploratory observation with no isolated comparison or long-term measurement.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed exploratory note reports that archive retrieval found earlier versions of ideas being treated as new in a later discussion. The result corrected a novelty claim; a single unblinded exercise does not establish improved cognition or discovery.
records.title: A useful correction to apparent novelty

records.date_label: Conversation summary dated 2026-10-09 in America/Chicago
records.epistemic_status: Summary-level evidence of a stated plan; not proof every planned step shipped together.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed conversation summary records an intention to prioritize a narrow reproducible demonstration: preserve source provenance, show a correction, and recover supported state later. This was a packaging plan; the published reader, private acquisition, and historical replay have distinct evidence scopes.
records.title: Choose one demonstrable loop

records.date_label: Published project method; adoption date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Documented reasoning method and explicit implementation boundary.
records.summary: The published project method starts by recovering relevant history and uncertainty, tests the favored interpretation, and carries forward what survives while keeping it revisable. This describes a working method; the small public reader does not implement the entire research system.
records.title: Recover, challenge, reconstruct

records.date_label: Published distribution boundary; decision date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Published package scope; broader private-release permission is separate.
records.summary: The public project account separates reusable continuity machinery from personal history. Fictional demonstration evidence provides a way to inspect a bounded mechanism while the founder's private biography stays outside the distributed reader.
records.title: Let the mechanism travel

records.date_label: Conceptual note documented 2026-09-28; original discussion date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Stored conceptual inference; no empirical growth metric established.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed conceptual record distinguishes accumulating changes from becoming more able to respond to future evidence. It treats revising or discarding a once-useful lesson as part of growth, rather than assuming that more retained material is always better.
records.title: Growth includes revising the lesson

records.date_label: Conceptual note documented 2026-09-28; original discussion date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Stored conceptual inference and proposed reasoning practice.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed discussion questions labels that sound neutral while hiding value judgments. The proposed practice is to explain what a pattern enables or costs, whose interests are affected, and which time horizon matters, while leaving those judgments open to challenge.
records.title: Name the values in the recommendation

records.date_label: Earlier conceptual note revisited 2026-10-17
records.epistemic_status: Documented research hypothesis; no governing state or permission change.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: Reviewed conceptual notes challenge the assumption that continuity must demand constant change or familiar behavior. They propose preserving room to revise, stay with a commitment, or refuse a change; this is a tentative design principle, not evidence of AI autonomy.
records.title: Room to change, remain, or decline

records.date_label: Published component; release date not established in this review
records.epistemic_status: Public component and retained verification reports; not executed again for this review.
records.summary: The published Continuity Reader is a rule-based offline component using fictional evidence. Its documented demonstration recovers a source-qualified comparison in a separate process with provenance, uncertainty, and no action authority; it contains no language model or authenticated Bee adapter.
records.title: A small reader that can be inspected

records.date_label: Bounded operation dated 2026-10-11 in the public ledger
records.epistemic_status: Attributed retained operation report; private receipt not inspected for this review.
records.summary: The public evidence ledger reports one founder-authorized Bee acquisition on October 11 followed by recovery in a distinct process. That bounded result supports acquisition and recovery of one selected observation; it does not establish synchronization, source changes, or general compatibility.
records.title: One bounded real-source recovery

records.date_label: Published evidence ledger; compilation date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Documented evidence classification, not a new test result.
records.summary: The published claims ledger distinguishes fictional test results, one real-source acquisition, and replay of historical corrections. These are separate artifacts with separate limitations; combining them into a single claim would overstate what was demonstrated.
records.title: A proof keeps its own boundaries

records.date_label: Conversation summary dated 2026-10-16 in America/Chicago
records.epistemic_status: Summary-level evidence of a future vision; no lifetime capability demonstrated.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed conversation summary explores preserving the context behind decisions and experiences across a life, beyond a collection of facts or photographs. This is a stated legacy vision, not a demonstrated lifetime model or a replacement for a person.
records.title: A lifetime view is a future possibility

records.date_label: Published future direction; delivery date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Future design possibility, not a deployed legacy service.
records.summary: The public roadmap imagines a person revisiting changing meaning and choosing what to retain. It places that possibility under personal control rather than assuming complete capture or allowing a system to decide what a life meant.
records.title: The person chooses what to preserve

records.date_label: Conversation summary dated 2026-10-16 in America/Chicago
records.epistemic_status: Summary-level evidence of an intended visualization, not an implementation inventory.

sources.title: Founder continuity record — private source reviewed

records.summary: A reviewed conversation summary proposes a visual command center connecting projects, responsibilities, dependencies, and timing. It offers a possible way to navigate daily context; the proposal does not establish that every displayed relationship is implemented or causal.
records.title: Connections can make context visible

records.date_label: Open research question; evaluation date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Research hypothesis; founder experience and synthetic work do not establish superiority.
records.summary: The public roadmap asks whether sustained accountable collaboration can help people reach useful possibilities they would be less likely to find through disconnected interactions. The proposed advantage remains unmeasured and independently unproven.
records.title: Does continuity help discovery?

records.date_label: Future product goal; delivery date unspecified
records.epistemic_status: Future product scope, not a shipped new-user experience.
records.summary: The longer-term product goal is a person-governed continuity core that grows around a new user's own sources, corrections, and permissions. Independent setup, bounded recovery, and adaptation for that person remain part of the product challenge beyond the small reader.
records.title: An empty starting point for someone else

records.date_label: Published limitation; independent verification pending
records.epistemic_status: Documented verification limit; no new compatibility test performed.
records.summary: The public documentation reports clean-extraction checks on the development Windows computer and explicitly states that a second physical computer has not independently verified the candidates. Broader compatibility remains an open evidence gap.
records.title: Repeatability beyond the development computer
